source.text: *ወ*መንፈሰ፡ ለዝናም፡ ሶበ፡ ይትሐወስ፡ እምመዝገበ፡ ዚአሁ፡ ይመጽኡ፡ መላእክት፡ ወያርኅዉ፡ መዝገበ፡ ወያወጽእዎ፡ ወሶበ፡ ይዘራእ፡ ዲበ፡ ኵሉ፡ የብስ፡ ይትኀበር፡ ምስለ፡ ማየ፡ ዘዲበ፡ የብስ፡ *ወሶበ፡ ይትኀበር፡ በኵሉ፡ ጊዜ፡ ምስለ፡ ማየ፡ ዘዲበ፡ የብስ።....

translation.text: When the wind of rain is stirred from its storehouse, angels come and open the storehouse and bring it out. When it is scattered over all dry land, it joins the water on dry land; and whenever it joins the water on dry land… [The conclusion is missing in the selected text.][a]

footnotes.text: Not ready for publication pending independent critical review: the selected print ends with four dots, and Charles printed107 note42 explicitly says the sentence’s apodosis, its completing main clause, is lost. The English translates the extant conditional fragment and labels its missing conclusion instead of inventing one. That label is modern explanation, not ancient wording and not a claim that the ancient book was deliberately left unfinished. No complete manuscript survey is claimed.
